title: Traducción de las voces de la lista N.2 a las lenguas cabécara, viceyta y lean-mulia (Colegio de Jesús Crucificado, Talamanca)
modern_id: Cabécar (cabe1245); Bribri (brib1243); Lean/Mulia = unclear Talamancan group (possibly Teribe/Naso-related)
size: c. 445-item Catherine II list x3 languages, ~11 fols
evidence: Oropesa TFM: 'triple traducción en lenguas castellana-cabecara (cabécar), castellana-viceyta y castellana-lean-mulia', sent by fr. José Olavarrieta 22 Aug 1789
novelty_basis: Campillo Pardo 2024 and Oropesa 2016 list it; García Aranda 2021 edits Guatemalan lists (coverage of Costa Rican lists unclear); Wikipedia Bribri cites a 1788-90 viceyta vocabulary, so at least the Bribri column is known. 'Lean-Mulia' column: no linguistic study found.
language_status: Bribri/Cabécar well documented today; Lean/Mulia unidentified, possibly extinct
notes: Catalogue (PARES 7287919) returned 502 during check; verified via TFM and Campillo Pardo 2024 description. The Lean-Mulia column is the item to check first.

title: Traducción de las voces de la lista N.2 a la lengua térrava (Térraba)
shelfmark_or_id: Indiferente 1342A, n.1 (sent separately with Olavarrieta letter, fol. 294v)
evidence: Olavarrieta: 'enbiar por separado la nómina de la lengua térrava, pues siendo la reducción más distante' (Oropesa TFM)
novelty_basis: Not found cited in Constenla 2007 'La lengua de Térraba' search results; listed by Campillo Pardo 2024 ('idioma de Ferrava'). Need to check García Aranda 2021.
language_status: Térraba dialect extinct in Costa Rica (Naso Teribe survives in Panama)
notes: Very early for Térraba; probably the earliest substantial wordlist if unedited.

title: Diccionario de la lengua sáliba en los Llanos de Santiago de la Atalaya y Río Meta (with Arte and Doctrina)
evidence: Campillo Pardo 2024 n.53: 'El diccionario se conserva completo en el mismo expediente, imágenes 232 a 289'
novelty_basis: The 1790 Arte de la lengua sáliba (Macuco/Orocué) is on World Digital Library and cited on Wikipedia; no edition of the AGI Diccionario found; modern Sáliba dictionary (Dueñas & Gómez 2015) doesn't cite colonial mss.
notes: Sent by viceroy Ezpeleta from Meta missions.

title: Philippine translations of Catherine II list N.2 (Tagalog, Bicol, Cagayán/Ibanag, Pangasinán, Bisaya, Zambal)
language_as_named: tagalog; bicol; cagayán; pangasinán; bisaya; zámbala
modern_id: Tagalog, Central Bikol, Ibanag, Pangasinan, Cebuano/Visayan, Sambal
evidence: Oropesa TFM: 'vocabulario múltiple ... castellana-bisaya ... y castellana-zámbala'; Manila 20 Dec 1788
novelty_basis: Studied by Rebeca Fernández Rodríguez, Historiographia Linguistica 42 (2015), 'A contrastive study of 18th-century word-lists'.
notes: Zambal column may deserve attention if not covered in Fernández Rodríguez.
